messages:
incident-bot: Paging: P1 -> runtime latency spike detected for hosted inference in us-west-2. Symptoms: 95th pct latency up from 180ms -> 1.6s, increased 5xx rate on gpu-pool-3. Auto-escalation to on-call — maria@redwood is paged.

maria: seeing it, joining. looking at console now.

maria: topline from console: latency spike started ~5m after today's deploy, traffic shifted to canary-2 by traffic-split rule.

sean: fyi I can repro higher p95 on dev against same model variant. kernel selection falling back to generic kernels, and batching seems to stall.

raj: pinging runtime logs + kube events for eviction/throttling.

alex: noticed increased queue depth on worker pods, logs show continuous kernel fallback warnings:
```
W runtime/kernel_selector.cc: fallback to cpu_kernel for op=attention because cuda kernel failed: out_of_memory? rc=-9
```

maria: interesting — OOM? but GPU mem usage on nodes looks normal. could be a new kernel not compiled for that binary.

sean: also seeing blocked batch flushes; batcher backlog length jumps and doesn't drain. suspect a regression in batching commit rolled in this morning (commit sha: d4f7b9e).

deploy-bot: deploy d4f7b9e -> prod completed 00:07:03 ago (canary traffic 10%).

maria: ok, mitigation options: 1) kill the canary feature flag to stop routing to new runtime, 2) rollback the canary deploy, 3) apply emergency hotfix to batching path. Any perf penalty acceptable short-term.

raj: confirm that kill-switch exists: rfctl patch-feature --env=prod --flag=canary-serving --off

alex: before toggling, grab connection dumps and prefix-KV stats. we need traces to tell if it's batching logic or kernel mapping.

maria: doing quick capture:
```
rcp run trace-collect --pool=gpu-pool-3 --duration=60s --out=/tmp/trace-1874200000.tgz
kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n prod --since=2m > /tmp/runtime-logs.txt
```

sre-rotations: copying logs to incident channel. link: https://internal.artifacts/1874200000/trace.tgz

cs-liaison: heads-up — CS: a handful of customers (acct: Acme, beta:chatplay) reported degraded responses, opening support tickets. prioritizing for SLA.

maria: toggling feature flag to stop canary routing now to reduce customer impact.

maria: run: `rfctl patch-feature --env=prod --flag=canary-serving --off`

incident-bot: Feature flag update: canary-serving -> OFF (propagated in 18s). Traffic rebalanced to stable pool.

sean: immediate telemetry looks better; p95 dropping back to ~210ms. 5xx rate trending down.

raj: kube events show a flurry of node-level kernel module version mismatches right after the deploy; some pods restarted and rejoined with older runtime image.

alex: digging: the build pipeline produced two artifact tags for d4f7b9e (builder race). some nodes pulled tag a and some tag b; tag b lacks optimized kernels, causing runtime to fallback.

maria: summary: bad rollout (artifact inconsistency) caused heterogeneous fleet; nodes without optimized kernels forced kernel fallback causing batching stalls and latency spike.

raj: mitigation path: 1) keep canary off 2) mark affected nodes drained for rollout 3) schedule uniform redeploy of runtime image with correct tag 4) consider rolling restart on gpu-pool-3 5) postmortem and release gating added.

sean: agree. also need short-term customer communication. cs-liaison please update Acme & chatplay with ETA ~30-45m while we redeploy.

cs-liaison: on it. sending templated message: "We observed elevated latency after a deployment; we've paused canary routing and are actively redeploying a fix. Next update in 30m." :mailbox_with_mail:

maria: initiating redeploy to enforce correct tag (command):
```
deploy-bot: start-rolling-restart --pool=gpu-pool-3 --image=runtime:d4f7b9e-stable --parallel=2
```

deploy-bot: Rolling restart started for gpu-pool-3. Expected completion ~20m.

raj: draining node gpu-3a-12 to evict stale pods: `kubectl drain gpu-3a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

alex: adding a temporary alert rule to catch kernel fallback spikes:
```
alert: KernelFallbackSurge
expr: increase(runtime_kernel_fallback_total[2m]) > 5
for: 1m
```

maria: handing off to raj for next hour to watch rollout and confirm stability. I'm stepping off the page.

raj: taking over. will post timeline + completion.

sean: QA note: add a preflight to build pipeline to assert kernel artifact parity across registries: `sha256 checks across images`.

maria: agreed — add gating job and a release checklist item: "verify kernel artifacts consistent across mirrors".

sre-rotations: posting runbook link for redeploy and monitoring checklist: https://runbooks/redwood/redeploy-runtime.md

raj: redeploy progress: 6/12 pods restarted, p95 already down to 195ms. no new fallbacks logged.

deploy-bot: Rolling restart progress: 50% complete.

cs-liaison: customer update sent. Acme acknowledged and asked to be notified when fully resolved.

raj: completed rolling restart. verifying over 10m window: p95 stable 180-220ms, 5xx rate back to baseline.

raj: closing mitigation: canary-serving remains OFF until release gating fixed.

maria: opened follow-up ticket ENG-8763 to add build parity checks + release checklist change.

alex: opened PR to pipeline: enforce image tag immutability and checksum verification.

sean: small postmortem notes: root cause = artifact race producing inconsistent runtime images; cascade = kernel fallback -> batching stalls -> latency spike; mitigation = kill canary, redeploy stable image, add gating.

cs-liaison: CS will follow up with affected customers with incident summary once postmortem is ready.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> Resolved (mitigated). Summary available in #postmortems once write-up completed.

maria: thanks everyone. great response. :thumbsup:

raj: thanks — monitoring for 2 more hours then I'll hand back to oncall rotation.

sre-rotations: noting oncall handoff: raj -> next oncall (sean) at 02:30 UTC.

sean: acknowledged, will take next watch.

alex: PR and pipeline tests are in review. target: prevent recurrence.

cs-liaison: will keep customers posted.

maria: final note: link to collected traces/logs: https://internal.artifacts/1874200000/summary.md

raj: closing thread, will file full postmortem in ~24h.
